scope: execution-required KVM guest-control qga runtime-handshake diagnosis

findings.guest_result: The new guest-side runtime diagnoser stopped existing qga processes, relaunched qga on the exact openable `...&02...` path with `-v -l`, and confirmed the selected path plus a live process.
The retained console capture shows the qga logfile tail collapsing to repeated `debug: dispatch` entries rather than an explicit open-path or startup error.
The same retained console capture ends with `=== APPLICATION EVENTS ===` followed by `NO_RECENT_MATCHING_EVENTS`.

findings.command: virsh qemu-agent-command ... guest-ping ; virsh qemu-monitor-command ... --hmp 'info chardev'
findings.host_result: After the runtime-handshake probe, host-side `guest-ping` still returned `Guest agent is not responding: QEMU guest agent is not connected` and HMP still reported the qga chardev as `disconnected`.

conclusion: The remaining KVM guest-control blocker now looks like a silent post-launch qga stall rather than path discovery. On the guest, the exact-path runtime probe only surfaces repeated `debug: dispatch` log lines and no recent matching Windows Application events, while the host still sees the qga channel as disconnected.
